// Runs on gemini.google.com. If the service worker stashed a prompt, type it
// into Gemini's input and hit send. If Gemini's DOM has changed and we can't
// find the box, fall back to a copy-and-paste toast so it never fails silently.
(() => {
  const PENDING_KEY = 'pendingGeminiPrompt';
  const MAX_AGE_MS = 10 * 60 * 1000; // ignore a stash older than 10 min

  // Ordered fallbacks: first match wins, so one Google rename doesn't kill it.
  const EDITOR_SELECTORS = [
    'rich-textarea .ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]',
    '.ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]',
    'div[contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"]',
    'div[contenteditable="true"]',
    'textarea',
  ];
  const SEND_SELECTORS = [
    'button.send-button',
    'button[aria-label*="send" i]',
    'button[mattooltip*="send" i]',
    'button[data-test-id="send-button"]',
  ];

  const sleep = (ms) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
  const isVisible = (el) => !!(el && (el.offsetWidth || el.offsetHeight || el.getClientRects().length));

  function findFirst(selectors, { mustBeEnabled = false } = {}) {
    for (const sel of selectors) {
      for (const el of document.querySelectorAll(sel)) {
        if (!isVisible(el)) continue;
        if (mustBeEnabled && (el.disabled || el.getAttribute('aria-disabled') === 'true')) continue;
        return el;
      }
    }
    return null;
  }

  async function waitFor(selectors, timeoutMs, opts) {
    const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs;
    while (Date.now() < deadline) {
      const el = findFirst(selectors, opts);
      if (el) return el;
      await sleep(200);
    }
    return null;
  }

  function fillEditor(editor, text) {
    editor.focus();
    if (editor.tagName === 'TEXTAREA') {
      editor.value = text;
      editor.dispatchEvent(new Event('input', { bubbles: true }));
      return;
    }
    // contenteditable: execCommand keeps frameworks (Quill) in sync best.
    try {
      document.execCommand('selectAll', false, null);
      document.execCommand('insertText', false, text);
    } catch {
      /* fall through */
    }
    if (!editor.textContent || !editor.textContent.trim()) {
      editor.textContent = text;
      editor.dispatchEvent(new InputEvent('input', { bubbles: true, data: text, inputType: 'insertText' }));
    }
  }

  function clickEl(el) {
    el.click();
    // Belt and suspenders for Material buttons that want real pointer events.
    for (const type of ['pointerdown', 'mousedown', 'mouseup', 'pointerup']) {
      el.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent(type, { bubbles: true }));
    }
  }

  function showFallbackToast(prompt) {
    if (document.getElementById('ytgs-toast')) return;
    const box = document.createElement('div');
    box.id = 'ytgs-toast';
    box.style.cssText = [
      'position:fixed', 'right:16px', 'bottom:16px', 'z-index:2147483647',
      'width:340px', 'max-width:calc(100vw - 32px)', 'background:#1f1f1f',
      'color:#fff', 'border:1px solid #444', 'border-radius:12px', 'padding:14px',
      'box-shadow:0 8px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.45)', 'font:13px/1.4 system-ui,sans-serif',
    ].join(';');
    box.innerHTML =
      '<div style="font-weight:600;margin-bottom:6px">Could not auto-fill Gemini</div>' +
      '<div style="opacity:.85;margin-bottom:8px">Copy this prompt and paste it (Cmd/Ctrl+V).</div>';
    const ta = document.createElement('textarea');
    ta.readOnly = true;
    ta.value = prompt;
    ta.style.cssText = 'width:100%;height:90px;resize:vertical;border-radius:8px;border:1px solid #555;background:#111;color:#eee;padding:8px;box-sizing:border-box';
    const row = document.createElement('div');
    row.style.cssText = 'display:flex;gap:8px;margin-top:8px;justify-content:flex-end';
    const copy = document.createElement('button');
    copy.textContent = 'Copy';
    const dismiss = document.createElement('button');
    dismiss.textContent = 'Dismiss';
    for (const b of [copy, dismiss]) {
      b.style.cssText = 'padding:6px 12px;border-radius:8px;border:0;cursor:pointer;font:inherit';
    }
    copy.style.background = '#8ab4f8';
    copy.style.color = '#202124';
    dismiss.style.background = '#3c3c3c';
    dismiss.style.color = '#fff';
    copy.addEventListener('click', async () => {
      try {
        await navigator.clipboard.writeText(prompt); // user gesture → allowed
        copy.textContent = 'Copied ✓';
      } catch {
        ta.focus();
        ta.select();
        document.execCommand('copy');
        copy.textContent = 'Copied ✓';
      }
    });
    dismiss.addEventListener('click', () => box.remove());
    row.append(copy, dismiss);
    box.append(ta, row);
    document.body.appendChild(box);
  }

  async function run() {
    const data = await chrome.storage.session.get(PENDING_KEY);
    const pending = data[PENDING_KEY];
    if (!pending) return;
    if (Date.now() - pending.ts > MAX_AGE_MS) {
      await chrome.storage.session.remove(PENDING_KEY);
      return;
    }

    const editor = await waitFor(EDITOR_SELECTORS, 20000);
    if (!editor) {
      // No editor on a /app page means the selectors broke → show the fallback.
      // On a login/loading page, leave the stash so the post-login load retries.
      if (location.pathname.startsWith('/app')) {
        await chrome.storage.session.remove(PENDING_KEY);
        showFallbackToast(pending.prompt);
      }
      return;
    }

    // Claim it now (editor only exists on the real app page) so a second Gemini
    // tab can't re-send the same prompt.
    await chrome.storage.session.remove(PENDING_KEY);

    try {
      fillEditor(editor, pending.prompt);
      const send = await waitFor(SEND_SELECTORS, 8000, { mustBeEnabled: true });
      if (send) {
        clickEl(send);
      } else {
        showFallbackToast(pending.prompt); // filled but couldn't find send
      }
    } catch {
      showFallbackToast(pending.prompt);
    }
  }

  run().catch(() => {});
})();

    button.textContent = label;
    button.setAttribute("aria-label", label);

        event.stopPropagation();
        if (event.stopImmediatePropagation) {

            return;

          return;

    card.appendChild(button);
    attachCardHoverHandlers(card, button);
    card.dataset[DATASET_FLAG] = "true";

    if (!(actions instanceof HTMLElement)) {
      return;
    }
    if (reconcileWatchButtons(actions)) {

    }

    button.type = "button";
    button.className = WATCH_BUTTON_CLASS;
    const label = getButtonLabel(currentLanguage);
    button.textContent = label;

      try {
        event.preventDefault();
        event.stopPropagation();
        if (event.stopImmediatePropagation) {
          event.stopImmediatePropagation();

        if (!canUseRuntime()) {

          chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: "OPEN_GEMINI", payload }, () => {

                markExtensionUnavailable();
                return;
              }
              logWarn("Failed to send OPEN_GEMINI message.", error);

          });
        } catch (error) {

            return;
          }
          throw error;
        }
      } catch (error) {
        if (isExtensionContextInvalidated(error)) {
          markExtensionUnavailable();
          return;
        }
        logError("Failed to handle summary click.", error);
      }

  const scanCards = () => {
    if (!extensionAvailable) {
      return;
    }
    try {
      const cards = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(CARD_SELECTORS));
      for (let index = cards.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
        const card = cards[index];
        if (!(card instanceof HTMLElement)) {
          continue;
        }
        if (card.dataset[DATASET_FLAG] === "true") {
          const existingButton = card.querySelector(`.${BUTTON_CLASS}`);
          if (existingButton instanceof HTMLButtonElement) {
            attachCardHoverHandlers(card, existingButton);
          }
          continue;
        }
        const existingButton = card.querySelector(`.${BUTTON_CLASS}`);
        if (existingButton instanceof HTMLButtonElement) {
          card.dataset[DATASET_FLAG] = "true";
          attachCardHoverHandlers(card, existingButton);
          continue;
        }
        if (hasInjectedAncestor(card)) {
          continue;
        }
        const url = extractUrl(card);
        if (!url) {
          continue;

        createButton(card);
      }
    } catch (error) {
      logWarn("Failed to scan YouTube cards.", error);
    }
  };

  const scanWatchButton = () => {
    if (!extensionAvailable) {
      return;
    }
    if (!isWatchPage()) {
      return;
    }
    const actions = getWatchActionsContainer();
    if (!actions) {
      return;
    }
    createWatchButton(actions);
  };

  const attachCardHoverHandlers = (card, button) => {
    if (!(card instanceof HTMLElement)) {
      return;
    }
    if (!(button instanceof HTMLButtonElement)) {
      return;
    }
    if (card.dataset[HOVER_BOUND_FLAG] === "true") {
      return;
    }
    card.dataset[HOVER_BOUND_FLAG] = "true";
    const getButton = () => card.querySelector(`.${BUTTON_CLASS}`);
    const show = () => {
      const activeButton = getButton();
      if (activeButton instanceof HTMLButtonElement) {
        activeButton.classList.add(BUTTON_VISIBLE_CLASS);
      }
    };
    const hide = (event) => {
      const related = event.relatedTarget;
      if (related instanceof Node && card.contains(related)) {
        return;
      }
      const activeButton = getButton();
      if (activeButton instanceof HTMLButtonElement) {
        activeButton.classList.remove(BUTTON_VISIBLE_CLASS);
      }
    };
    card.addEventListener("mouseover", show);
    card.addEventListener("mouseout", hide);

  const scanAll = () => {
    scanCards();
    scanWatchButton();
  };

  const scheduleScan = throttle(scanAll, THROTTLE_MS);
  const observer = new MutationObserver(() => scheduleScan());
  try {
    observer.observe(document.documentElement, { childList: true, subtree: true });
  } catch (error) {
    logWarn("Failed to observe DOM mutations.", error);
  }
  window.addEventListener("yt-navigate-finish", scheduleScan);
  window.addEventListener("yt-page-data-updated", scheduleScan);

    .then((settings) => {
      applyHoverMode(settings.showButtonOnHoverOnly);
      updateLanguage(settings.language);
    })
    .catch((error) => {
      logWarn("Failed to apply hover mode from settings.", error);
      applyHoverMode(DEFAULT_SETTINGS.showButtonOnHoverOnly);
    });

  if (chrome?.storage?.onChanged) {
    chrome.storage.onChanged.addListener((changes, areaName) => {
      try {
        if (areaName !== "local") {
          return;
        }
        const updated = changes?.[SETTINGS_KEY]?.newValue;
        if (updated && typeof updated === "object") {
          if (
            Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(
              updated,
              "showButtonOnHoverOnly"
            )
          ) {
            applyHoverMode(updated.showButtonOnHoverOnly);
          }
          if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(updated, "language")) {
            updateLanguage(updated.language);
          }
        }
      } catch (error) {
        logWarn("Failed to handle settings change.", error);
      }
    });
  }

  scheduleScan();
})();

import {
  getDefaultPromptTemplate,
  getDefaultSettings,
  SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES,
} from "../shared/constants.js";
import { getSettings, setSettings } from "../shared/storage.js";

const form = document.getElementById("options-form");
const languageInput = document.getElementById("language");
const autoSendInput = document.getElementById("autoSend");
const openInNewTabInput = document.getElementById("openInNewTab");
const hoverOnlyInput = document.getElementById("showButtonOnHoverOnly");
const sendDelayInput = document.getElementById("sendDelayMs");
const promptTemplateInput = document.getElementById("promptTemplate");
const templateExampleBody = document.getElementById("templateExampleBody");
const resetButton = document.getElementById("resetButton");
const status = document.getElementById("status");

let statusTimer = null;
let lastLanguage = null;

const getMessage = (key, fallback = "") =>
  chrome?.i18n?.getMessage?.(key) || fallback;

const applyLocalization = () => {
  const uiLanguage = chrome?.i18n?.getUILanguage?.();
  if (uiLanguage) {
    document.documentElement.lang = uiLanguage;
    document.documentElement.dir = uiLanguage.toLowerCase().startsWith("ar")
      ? "rtl"
      : "ltr";
  }
  const nodes = document.querySelectorAll("[data-i18n]");
  nodes.forEach((node) => {
    const key = node.getAttribute("data-i18n");
    if (!key) {
      return;
    }
    const message = getMessage(key);
    if (message) {
      node.textContent = message;
    }
  });
};

const clamp = (value, min, max) => Math.min(Math.max(value, min), max);

const showStatus = (message) => {
  status.textContent = message;
  status.classList.add("is-visible");
  if (statusTimer) {
    clearTimeout(statusTimer);
  }
  statusTimer = setTimeout(() => {
    status.classList.remove("is-visible");
  }, 1500);
};

const SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE_SET = new Set(SUPPORTED_LANGUAGES);
const sanitizeLanguage = (value) =>
  SUPPORTED_LANGUAGE_SET.has(value) ? value : "en";

const normalizeDelay = (value, fallback) => {
  const parsed = Number.parseInt(value, 10);
  if (Number.isNaN(parsed)) {
    return fallback;
  }
  return clamp(parsed, 0, 2000);
};

const populateForm = (settings) => {
  const defaults = getDefaultSettings();
  const safe = { ...defaults, ...(settings || {}) };
  languageInput.value = sanitizeLanguage(safe.language);
  autoSendInput.checked = Boolean(safe.autoSend);
  openInNewTabInput.checked = Boolean(safe.openInNewTab);
  hoverOnlyInput.checked = Boolean(safe.showButtonOnHoverOnly);
  sendDelayInput.value = normalizeDelay(safe.sendDelayMs, defaults.sendDelayMs);
  promptTemplateInput.value = safe.promptTemplate || defaults.promptTemplate;
  lastLanguage = sanitizeLanguage(safe.language);
  updateTemplateExample(lastLanguage);
};

const readForm = () => {
  const defaults = getDefaultSettings();
  return {
    language: sanitizeLanguage(languageInput.value),
    autoSend: autoSendInput.checked,
    openInNewTab: openInNewTabInput.checked,
    showButtonOnHoverOnly: hoverOnlyInput.checked,
    sendDelayMs: normalizeDelay(sendDelayInput.value, defaults.sendDelayMs),
    promptTemplate: promptTemplateInput.value || defaults.promptTemplate,
  };
};

const updateTemplateExample = (language) => {
  if (!templateExampleBody) {
    return;
  }
  templateExampleBody.textContent = getDefaultPromptTemplate(language);
};

const handleLanguageChange = () => {
  const nextLanguage = sanitizeLanguage(languageInput.value);
  const previousLanguage = lastLanguage;
  const currentTemplate = promptTemplateInput.value.trim();
  const previousDefault = previousLanguage
    ? getDefaultPromptTemplate(previousLanguage)
    : "";
  if (!currentTemplate || (previousDefault && currentTemplate === previousDefault)) {
    promptTemplateInput.value = getDefaultPromptTemplate(nextLanguage);
  }
  updateTemplateExample(nextLanguage);
  lastLanguage = nextLanguage;
};

const handleSave = async (event) => {
  event.preventDefault();
  const payload = readForm();
  sendDelayInput.value = payload.sendDelayMs;
  await setSettings(payload);
  showStatus(getMessage("statusSaved", "Saved"));
};

const handleReset = async () => {
  const defaults = getDefaultSettings();
  await setSettings(defaults);
  populateForm(defaults);
  showStatus(getMessage("statusReset", "Reset to defaults"));
};

const init = async () => {
  applyLocalization();
  document.title = getMessage("optionsTitle", document.title);
  const settings = await getSettings();
  populateForm(settings);
};

form.addEventListener("submit", handleSave);
resetButton.addEventListener("click", handleReset);
languageInput.addEventListener("change", handleLanguageChange);
init().catch(() => populateForm(getDefaultSettings()));
```

```text
# YouTube → Gemini Summary (Chrome Extension)

Status: Production ready (v0.1.3)

## What it does
- Adds “🤖 Gemini ile özetle” button on YouTube video + Shorts cards.
- On click opens https://gemini.google.com/app, fills the prompt, and (optionally) auto-sends.

## How it works (high level)
- YouTube content script injects button and extracts URL/title/channel.
- Background service worker opens/reuses Gemini tab and sends a message.
- Gemini content script fills Quill editor (`.ql-editor.textarea.new-input-ui[contenteditable="true"]`) and clicks send (`button.send-button.submit`).

## Install (Developer mode / Load unpacked)
1. Open `chrome://extensions` in Chrome.
2. Enable Developer mode (top-right).
3. Click “Load unpacked” and select the project root folder.

## Usage
- Hover a YouTube card to reveal the button, then click.
- A Gemini tab opens and the summary starts (if Auto-send is enabled).

## Options
- Language: Stored setting for your prompt language; update the template accordingly.
- Auto-send: Automatically clicks send after filling the prompt.
- Open in new tab: When enabled, always opens a new Gemini tab.
- Hover-only: Show the button only on hover.
- Send delay: Wait time before clicking send (0-2000ms).
- Prompt template: Uses `{title}`, `{channel}`, `{url}` placeholders.

## Known limitations
- Gemini/YouTube DOM can change and may break automation.
- User must be signed into Gemini; if not, the prompt remains pending until sign-in.
- This is UI automation, not an official Gemini API integration.

## Security/Privacy notes
- No external servers.
- Only `chrome.storage.local` is used.
- URL/title/channel are stored locally as `pendingPrompt` only until sent.
- See [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md) for details.

## Contributing
- Issues and PRs are welcome.
- Run through [TEST_CHECKLIST.md](TEST_CHECKLIST.md) before releases.
- Packaging notes are in [RELEASE.md](RELEASE.md).
- Built with ChatGPT 5.2 Codex.

## License
MIT License. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
```

// Pure helpers shared by the service worker, the options page, and the tests.
// No DOM, no chrome.*, so it stays import-safe for `node --test`.

// Brief on purpose: let Gemini pick the structure, because it reads better than a
// heavily prescribed format. Edit it in the options page.
export const DEFAULT_PROMPT = `Summarize the video:`;

// YouTube video ids are exactly 11 url-safe chars.
const VIDEO_ID = /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$/;

// Return the canonical https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID for any YouTube video
// URL (watch, youtu.be, shorts, live, embed, m./music.). Returns null for
// anything that isn't a single YouTube video (channels, feeds, other sites).
export function canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(urlString) {
  let url;
  try {
    url = new URL(urlString);
  } catch {
    return null;
  }

  const host = url.hostname.replace(/^www\./, '');
  let id = null;

  if (host === 'youtu.be') {
    id = url.pathname.slice(1).split('/')[0];
  } else if (
    host === 'youtube.com' ||
    host === 'm.youtube.com' ||
    host === 'music.youtube.com'
  ) {
    if (url.pathname === '/watch') {
      id = url.searchParams.get('v');
    } else {
      const m = url.pathname.match(/^\/(?:shorts|live|embed|v)\/([^/?#]+)/);
      if (m) id = m[1];
    }
  } else {
    return null;
  }

  if (id && VIDEO_ID.test(id)) {
    return `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=${id}`;
  }
  return null;
}

// Clean a browser tab title into a video title: drop the leading "(3) " unread
// count YouTube adds and the trailing " - YouTube".
export function stripTitle(title) {
  return (title || '')
    .replace(/^\(\d+\)\s*/, '')
    .replace(/\s*-\s*YouTube\s*$/, '')
    .trim();
}

// Build the full Gemini prompt. The video title + link are always appended so
// the user's saved instructions never have to remember them.
export function buildPrompt(instructions, title, url) {
  const body = (instructions || DEFAULT_PROMPT).trim();
  const tail = title ? `${title}\n${url}` : url;
  return `${body}\n\n${tail}`;
}

// Tells the service worker the current YouTube URL so it can light up a green
// "ready" badge on the toolbar icon when you're on a video. YouTube is a single
// page app, so we report on first load and on every in-page navigation.
(() => {
  let last = null;

  function report() {
    if (location.href === last) return;
    last = location.href;
    try {
      chrome.runtime.sendMessage({ type: 'YT_URL', url: location.href });
    } catch {
      // service worker asleep or extension reloading, so the next nav retries.
    }
  }

  report();
  // YouTube fires this when it finishes an in-app navigation.
  window.addEventListener('yt-navigate-finish', report, true);
  window.addEventListener('yt-page-data-updated', report, true);
  // Belt-and-suspenders for history.pushState navigations.
  window.addEventListener('popstate', report);
})();
```

import { DEFAULT_PROMPT } from './lib.js';

const $prompt = document.getElementById('prompt');
const $status = document.getElementById('status');

function flash(msg) {
  $status.textContent = msg;
  setTimeout(() => {
    if ($status.textContent === msg) $status.textContent = '';
  }, 2000);
}

async function load() {
  const { instructions } = await chrome.storage.sync.get('instructions');
  $prompt.value = instructions || DEFAULT_PROMPT;
}

document.getElementById('save').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  await chrome.storage.sync.set({ instructions: $prompt.value });
  flash('Saved ✓');
});

document.getElementById('reset').addEventListener('click', async () => {
  $prompt.value = DEFAULT_PROMPT;
  await chrome.storage.sync.set({ instructions: DEFAULT_PROMPT });
  flash('Reset to default');
});

load();

```text
# YouTube Summary with Gemini

A tiny, open-source Chrome extension (Manifest V3). While you're watching a
YouTube video, click the toolbar button. It opens **Gemini** with a summary
prompt already filled in and sent, including the video's title and link.

The default prompt is intentionally short so Gemini picks a good structure; you
can edit it any time in the options page.

## Install (load unpacked)

The extension isn't on the Chrome Web Store yet, so install it from source:

1. Download or clone this repository.
2. Open `chrome://extensions`.
3. Turn on **Developer mode** (top-right).
4. Click **Load unpacked** and select the project folder.
5. Pin the extension (puzzle 🧩 icon → pin) so the toolbar button is visible.

You must be **signed into Gemini** in the same browser for auto-fill to work.

> The icons are committed, so there's nothing to build. If you ever need to
> regenerate them, run `python3 tools/make_icons.py` (standard library only).

## Use

- On a YouTube video, the toolbar icon shows a small **green dot** in the
  corner, and that means it's ready. Click it: a Gemini tab opens, the prompt is
  typed in and submitted, and the summary starts generating.
- Not on a YouTube video? No green dot, and clicking shows a brief `YT?` badge and
  does nothing.
- **Edit the prompt:** right-click the icon → **Options** (or `chrome://extensions`
  → Details → Extension options). The video's title and link are appended
  automatically, so your prompt never needs to mention them.

## How it works

- `content-youtube.js` runs on YouTube and reports the page URL to the service
  worker (on load and on YouTube's in-app navigations). The worker swaps the
  toolbar icon to the green-dot variant when you're on a video.
- `background.js` (service worker) reads the active tab's URL on click,
  canonicalizes it to `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID`, builds the prompt,
  stashes it in `chrome.storage.session`, and opens Gemini.
- `content-gemini.js` runs on Gemini, reads the stashed prompt, types it into the
  input box, and clicks send.

### The one fragile part

Gemini's web app has no official "prefill" URL, so auto-fill works by typing into
Gemini's input element directly, and Google can change that DOM without notice.
The content script uses **ordered fallback selectors**, and if it still can't find
the box it shows a **copy-and-paste toast** with the prompt. It degrades; it never
fails silently. If auto-fill ever stops working, update `EDITOR_SELECTORS` /
`SEND_SELECTORS` in `content-gemini.js`.

## Limitations

- Gemini can only watch **public** videos; private/unlisted ones fall back to the
  title and transcript if available.
- Requires being signed into Gemini with YouTube access enabled on the account.

## Develop

```bash
npm test                      # run the unit tests (node --test over test/)
python3 tools/make_icons.py   # regenerate the icons
```

`lib.js` holds the pure, testable logic (URL canonicalization, prompt building,
the default prompt) and is shared by the service worker, the options page, and the
tests.

## Package for distribution

```bash
bash tools/pack.sh
```

Produces, in `dist/` (gitignored):

- `yt-gemini-summary.zip`: upload to the Chrome Web Store (manifest at the zip
  root, runtime files only).
- `yt-gemini-summary.crx`: a signed package for self-distribution.

The first run creates `key.pem` (the signing key) and reuses it afterward, so the
extension ID stays stable across rebuilds. `key.pem`, `dist/`, and `*.crx` are
gitignored, so **never commit the key.** Note: Chrome blocks `.crx` files installed
outside the Web Store for normal users, so for everyday use either load unpacked
or publish to the Web Store with the `.zip`.

## Privacy

The extension sends **no data to the developer** and has **no analytics, tracking,
or ads**. The only thing transmitted is the prompt you send to **your own** Gemini
session. The current video's title and link are placed into that prompt for you.
Your saved prompt and a short-lived session handoff live only on your device. Full
details: [PRIVACY.md](PRIVACY.md).

## License

MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
```

```text
# Privacy Policy for YouTube Summary with Gemini

_Last updated: 2026-06-21_

YouTube Summary with Gemini is a Chrome extension (Manifest V3) that, on one click,
summarizes the YouTube video you are watching by opening Google Gemini and
auto-filling a summary prompt. It is built to be private by default.

## What it stores

The extension stores, **locally on your device** via Chrome's `storage` API:

- your editable summary prompt (so it persists between sessions), and
- a short-lived session handoff, the prompt it just built, so the freshly
  opened Gemini tab can read it. This is cleared with your browser session.

That's it. None of this is sent to the developer.

## What it sends: read this carefully

The extension sends **no data to the developer** and contains **no analytics,
telemetry, tracking, or ads**.

The only "transmission" is the core feature itself. When you click the button, the
current video's **title and link** are placed into a prompt. That prompt is then typed
into **your own, signed-in Google Gemini session** and submitted, exactly as if you had
typed it yourself. That prompt goes to Google Gemini under your account, governed by
Google's own privacy terms. The extension is not a party to it and keeps no copy on
any server (there is no server).

## What it accesses, and when

- It reads the **current tab's URL and title only when you click** the toolbar
  button (via `activeTab`), to identify the video.
- It detects when you are on a YouTube page so the toolbar icon can show the green
  "ready" dot (host access to youtube.com).
- It fills and submits the prompt on gemini.google.com (host access to that site).
- If Gemini's page layout changes and the prompt can't be auto-filled, it copies the
  prompt to your clipboard (`clipboardWrite`) so you can paste it. That is the only
  use of the clipboard.

## What it does NOT do

- No accounts, logins, or credentials are created or read by the extension.
- No analytics, telemetry, tracking, cookies, fingerprinting, or advertising.
- No data is collected by, or transmitted to, the developer or any third party.
- No data is sold or shared, and none is used for advertising or creditworthiness.
- No remote code: everything that runs is bundled in the extension.

## Open source

The full source code is public and MIT-licensed, so you can verify all of the above:
https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary

## Contact

Questions or concerns? Open an issue:
https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/issues
```
</details></tool-use>

# Chrome Web Store listing: YouTube Summary with Gemini

Everything needed for the developer-console listing. Copy/paste the text; upload the
images from `store-assets/images/`. Regenerate images with `npm run store-assets`.

---

## Product details

**Item name**
```
YouTube Summary with Gemini: Open Source One-Click Summarizer
```

**Summary** (short description, max 132 chars, and this one is 123)
```
One click summarizes the YouTube video you're watching in Gemini. Editable prompt, copy fallback, no tracking. Open source.
```

**Description** (detailed)
```
Watching a long YouTube video and want the gist first? YouTube Summary with Gemini adds one toolbar button: click it on any YouTube video and Gemini opens in a new tab with a summary prompt already filled in and sent — the video's title and link are added for you automatically.

That's the whole product. No dashboards, no accounts to create, no servers in the middle. You stay in your own Gemini session the entire time.

WHY YOU'LL LIKE IT
- One click: on any YouTube video, click the toolbar button and Gemini starts summarizing — title and link attached automatically.
- A green "ready" dot on the toolbar icon tells you at a glance when you're on a video the extension can summarize.
- Fully editable prompt: the default is a short "Summarize the video:" so Gemini picks a good structure, but you can rewrite it to analyze, critique, pull action items, or ask your own questions. Edit it any time on the options page.
- Never stuck: Gemini has no official prefill URL, so auto-fill types into Gemini's input directly. If Google changes that page, the extension falls back to a copy-to-clipboard toast with your prompt — it degrades, it never fails silently.
- Private by design: no analytics, no tracking, no ads, no data sent to the developer. The only thing transmitted is the prompt you send to your own Gemini session.
- Featherweight: vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, Manifest V3, no frameworks, no background polling.

HOW IT WORKS
On a YouTube video the extension reads the page URL and title only when you click. It builds your prompt (your instructions + the video's title and link), opens Gemini in a new tab, types the prompt into Gemini's input box, and sends it. Everything happens in your browser, in your signed-in Gemini session.

OPEN SOURCE (MIT)
YouTube Summary with Gemini is fully open source under the MIT license. Read the code, file an issue, or contribute:
https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary

GETTING STARTED
1) Install and pin the extension (puzzle icon → pin) so the toolbar button is visible.
2) Sign in to Gemini in the same browser.
3) Open any YouTube video and click the button. That's it.

Tip: want a different prompt? Right-click the icon → Options.

Made by Yi Li · https://yili.dev/projects/youtube_summary_with_gemini/
```

**Category:** Workflow & Planning
**Language:** English (United States)

---

## Privacy

**Single purpose**
```
On one click, summarize the YouTube video you are currently watching by opening Google Gemini and auto-filling a summary prompt with the video's title and link.
```

**Permission justifications**
- `storage`:
  ```
  Saves your editable summary prompt so it persists between sessions, and holds a short-lived session handoff (the built prompt) so the Gemini tab can read it after it opens. Nothing is sent to the developer.
  ```
- `activeTab`:
  ```
  When you click the toolbar button, reads only the current tab's URL and title to identify the YouTube video being summarized. No access to other tabs or to the page until you click.
  ```
- `clipboardWrite`:
  ```
  Powers the copy-to-clipboard fallback: if Gemini's page layout changes and the prompt can't be auto-filled, the extension copies the prompt so you can paste it yourself instead of being stuck.
  ```
- Host permission `https://www.youtube.com/*`, `https://m.youtube.com/*`:
  ```
  Detects when you are on a YouTube video so the toolbar icon can show the green "ready" dot and read the video's URL and title on click.
  ```
- Host permission `https://gemini.google.com/*`:
  ```
  Fills the summary prompt into Gemini's input box and submits it in your own signed-in Gemini session — the core function of the extension.
  ```
- Remote code: **No.**

**Data usage / certifications**: the extension does **not** collect or transmit any of the
disclosable data categories to the developer or any third party (no PII, location, financial,
authentication, web history, user activity, or website-content collection). The only "transmission"
is functional: the current video's title and link are placed into **your own** Gemini prompt, which
you send to Google Gemini in your own session. That is the core feature, not data collection. Your
saved prompt stays on your device. Certify all three: data is **not sold**, **not used for unrelated
purposes**, and **not used for creditworthiness/lending**.

**Privacy policy URL**
```
https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/PRIVACY.md
```

import test from 'node:test';
import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
import { canonicalizeYouTubeUrl, stripTitle, buildPrompt, DEFAULT_PROMPT } from '../lib.js';

const ID = 'dQw4w9WgXcQ';
const CANON = `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=${ID}`;

test('watch url strips extra params', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=${ID}&t=42s&list=abc`), CANON);
});

test('watch url without www', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://youtube.com/watch?v=${ID}`), CANON);
});

test('youtu.be short link', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://youtu.be/${ID}?si=xyz`), CANON);
});

test('shorts', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://www.youtube.com/shorts/${ID}`), CANON);
});

test('live', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://www.youtube.com/live/${ID}`), CANON);
});

test('embed', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://www.youtube.com/embed/${ID}`), CANON);
});

test('m.youtube watch', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=${ID}`), CANON);
});

test('music.youtube watch', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://music.youtube.com/watch?v=${ID}`), CANON);
});

test('non-video youtube page returns null', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl('https://www.youtube.com/feed/subscriptions'), null);
});

test('watch without v returns null', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl('https://www.youtube.com/watch?list=abc'), null);
});

test('malformed id returns null', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl('https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tooShort'), null);
});

test('non-youtube host returns null', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl(`https://example.com/watch?v=${ID}`), null);
});

test('garbage input returns null', () => {
  assert.equal(canonicalizeYouTubeUrl('not a url'), null);
});

test('stripTitle removes trailing - YouTube', () => {
  assert.equal(stripTitle('Great Talk - YouTube'), 'Great Talk');
});

test('stripTitle removes leading unread count', () => {
  assert.equal(stripTitle('(3) Great Talk - YouTube'), 'Great Talk');
});

test('stripTitle leaves a clean title alone', () => {
  assert.equal(stripTitle('Just A Title'), 'Just A Title');
});

test('buildPrompt appends title and url', () => {
  const out = buildPrompt('Summarize the video:', 'My Video', CANON);
  assert.match(out, /^Summarize the video:/);
  assert.match(out, /My Video/);
  assert.ok(out.includes(CANON));
});

test('buildPrompt puts the title line directly above the url', () => {
  const out = buildPrompt('Summarize the video:', 'My Video', CANON);
  assert.ok(out.endsWith(`My Video\n${CANON}`));
});

test('buildPrompt falls back to default when instructions empty', () => {
  const out = buildPrompt('', 'My Video', CANON);
  assert.ok(out.startsWith(DEFAULT_PROMPT.trim()));
});

test('buildPrompt without a title still includes the url', () => {
  const out = buildPrompt('Summarize the video:', '', CANON);
  assert.ok(out.endsWith(`\n\n${CANON}`));
});

test('DEFAULT_PROMPT is the brief one-liner', () => {
  assert.equal(DEFAULT_PROMPT, 'Summarize the video:');
});
```

## YouTube video support

- **Status:** The page marks the YouTube URL capability as `"Preview"` and says it is currently free. It does not identify the feature as GA.
- **Model example:** The documented request uses `"gemini-3.7-flash"`. The page gives no separate minimum-model requirement for YouTube URLs. Generally, it says all Gemini models support video input.
- **Access restrictions:** Only publicly accessible YouTube videos work; private and unlisted videos are excluded.
- **Video-count limits:**
  - Models older than Gemini 2.5: one video per request.
  - Gemini 2.5 and newer: up to 10 videos per request.
- **Tier limits:**
  - Free tier: up to 8 hours of YouTube video per day.
  - Paid tier: no limit tied to video length.
- **Request shape:** Send a POST to the Interactions endpoint with the API-key header and a JSON body containing a model plus an input array. The array includes text and a video object; the documented video object is `"type": "video", "uri": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9hE5-98ZeCg"`. SDKs use the equivalent `interactions.create` call.
- **Understanding features:** Gemini analyzes both sound and imagery, supports questions about particular moments, and accepts timestamps in `MM:SS` format. Visual sampling is generally one frame per second, so very fast action may be missed.
- **Page date:** Last updated 2026-08-26 UTC.
```

```text
| API | Signature | Behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `GM_setValue` | `GM_setValue(key, value)` | Synchronous storage write. Values must be JSON-serializable. |
| `GM.setValue` | `await GM.setValue(key, value)` | Promise-based alias for the write operation. |
| `GM_getValue` | `GM_getValue(key, defaultValue)` | Synchronously returns the stored value, or the fallback when absent. |
| `GM.getValue` | `await GM.getValue(key, defaultValue)` | Promise-based read with the same fallback behavior. |
| `GM_deleteValue` | `GM_deleteValue(key)` | Synchronously removes one stored key. |
| `GM.deleteValue` | `await GM.deleteValue(key)` | Promise-based deletion alias. |
| `GM_openInTab` | `GM_openInTab(url, optionsOrBackground)` | Opens a tab and returns `{ close, closed, onclose }`. A boolean means open in background; options support `active`, `insert`, `pinned`, and Firefox `container`. |
| `GM.openInTab` | `GM.openInTab(url, optionsOrBackground)` | `GM.*` alias; documented without async behavior, so use its tab-control object directly. |
| `GM_registerMenuCommand` | `GM_registerMenuCommand(caption, onClick, options?)` | Synchronously adds a popup command. The handler receives the activating event. Options include `id`, `icon`, `title`, and `autoClose`. |
| `GM.registerMenuCommand` | `GM.registerMenuCommand(caption, onClick, options?)` | `GM.*` compatibility alias; documented without Promise behavior. |

For one script matching both YouTube and Gemini:

- `GM_*` forms are the legacy, synchronous style.
- `GM.*` forms are Greasemonkey 4-compatible aliases; storage operations are asynchronous.
- Values belong to the userscript, so use site-specific key names if YouTube and Gemini data must remain separate.
- `GM_openInTab` and menu registration remain directly usable without `await` according to the provided documentation.

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/storage`

```text
- **`chrome.storage.local`**: Data stays on the individual machine and is removed when the extension is uninstalled. It is exposed to content scripts by default; `setAccessLevel()` can restrict that access.
- **`chrome.storage.sync`**: When Chrome Sync is enabled, data synchronizes to the user’s other signed-in Chrome browsers, so it is not device-local only. When Sync is disabled, it behaves like local storage. Content-script access is enabled by default and can be changed with `setAccessLevel()`.
- **`chrome.storage.session`**: Data is held in memory only and is not written to disk. It is cleared when the extension is disabled, reloaded, updated, or Chrome restarts. Content scripts cannot access it by default; `setAccessLevel()` can enable broader access.

Therefore, the claim that `storage.sync` is only local is **false unless synchronization is disabled**.
```
</details></tool-use>

### YouTube card selectors

- `ytd-rich-item-renderer`
- `ytd-video-renderer`
- `ytd-grid-video-renderer`
- `ytm-shorts-lockup-view-model-v2`
- `yt-lockup-view-model`
- `ytd-compact-video-renderer`
- `ytd-playlist-panel-video-renderer`

### Watch-page action selectors

Tried in this order:

- `ytd-watch-metadata #actions-inner ytd-menu-renderer #top-level-buttons-computed`
- `ytd-watch-metadata ytd-menu-renderer #top-level-buttons-computed`
- `ytd-watch-metadata #top-level-buttons-computed`

Additional lookup and fallback:

- `ytd-watch-metadata ytd-menu-renderer`
- `#top-level-buttons-computed`
- `ytd-watch-metadata #actions-inner`

For the fallback container, the script checks `#menu`; it inserts the extension container before that element, or prepends it to the actions area.

### SPA observation and events

- A `MutationObserver` watches `document.documentElement` with `childList: true` and `subtree: true`.
- Mutation callbacks trigger a scan throttled to 200 ms.
- The same scan runs on `yt-navigate-finish` and `yt-page-data-updated`.
- An initial scan is scheduled immediately.
- Card scanning handles dynamically added content; watch-page scanning requires either a `/watch` path or `ytd-watch-metadata`.

### Button insertion

- Card buttons are appended directly to the matched card element.
- The watch button is prepended to the resolved action container.
- Duplicate watch buttons are removed, and an existing primary button is moved into the current action container.
- Card buttons receive hover handlers; the configured hover-only mode is applied through the `gemini-hover-only` document class.

### Card metadata selectors

**Video URL**

The first `a[href]` whose path starts with `/watch` or `/shorts` is used. The search includes the card, its `shadowRoot`, and its `renderRoot`.

**Title, in order**

- `a.yt-lockup-metadata-view-model__title span`
- `a[aria-label]`
- `a[href^="/shorts"] span`
- The selected video anchor’s `title` attribute
- The selected video anchor’s text

**Channel, in order**

- `a[href^="/@"]`
- `a[href^="/channel/"]`
- `a[href^="/c/"]`
- `a[href^="/user/"]`
- `#channel-name a, ytd-channel-name a`

### Watch-page metadata selectors

**Title, in order**

- `ytd-watch-metadata h1 yt-formatted-string`
- `ytd-watch-metadata h1`
- `ytd-watch-metadata #title yt-formatted-string`
- `ytd-watch-metadata #title`
- `meta[name="title"]`
- `meta[property="og:title"]`
- The document title after removing its YouTube suffix

**Channel, in order**

- `ytd-watch-metadata #owner #channel-name a`
- `ytd-watch-metadata ytd-channel-name a`
- `ytd-video-owner-renderer #channel-name a`
- `ytd-video-owner-renderer ytd-channel-name a`
- `ytd-watch-metadata #channel-name`
- `ytd-video-owner-renderer #channel-name`

### Error and fallback behavior

- Missing or invalid metadata produces empty fields; missing URLs prevent button creation or message sending.
- Storage read failures use default settings and log a warning.
- Runtime messaging failures are logged.
- If the extension context is invalidated, all extension buttons are disabled and marked unavailable until the page is reloaded.
- Observer, settings, language, hover-mode, scan, and click-handler failures are caught and logged rather than stopping the script.
```
</details></tool-use>

<tool-use data-tool-type="read" data-tool-name="WebFetch"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **WebFetch**</summary>
 `https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/content-gemini.js`

```text
- **Injection context:** A script runs on `gemini.google.com`, reads `pendingGeminiPrompt` from `chrome.storage.session`, and processes the stored `{ prompt, ts }`.
- **Editor selector order:**
  1. `rich-textarea .ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]`
  2. `.ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]`
  3. `div[contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"]`
  4. `div[contenteditable="true"]`
  5. `textarea`
- **Send selector order:**
  1. `button.send-button`
  2. `button[aria-label*="send" i]`
  3. `button[mattooltip*="send" i]`
  4. `button[data-test-id="send-button"]`
- **Waiting:** Visible elements are polled every 200 ms. The editor wait lasts up to 20 seconds; the enabled send-button wait lasts up to 8 seconds.
- **Filling:** Textareas receive a value plus an `input` event. Contenteditable editors are focused and filled with `execCommand`; if that fails, text content and an input event are used.
- **Pending deletion:** An expired item is removed immediately. Once an editor is found, the item is removed before filling or sending, preventing duplicate submission by another Gemini tab.
- **Auto-submit:** If an enabled send control appears, the script clicks it and also dispatches pointer and mouse events. If no send control appears, it shows the fallback toast.
- **Stale and login behavior:** Items older than 10 minutes are discarded. If no editor appears, an `/app` page triggers deletion plus the toast; other pages, including login/loading pages, retain the item for a later retry.
- **Clipboard fallback UX:** The toast contains the prompt in a read-only textarea and offers Copy and Dismiss. Copy first uses `navigator.clipboard.writeText`; if that fails, it selects the textarea and invokes `document.execCommand('copy')`, then changes the button label to `Copied ✓`.
```
</details></tool-use>

## 2. `ipekbayrak/yt-gemini-summary`

### Permissions and privacy

**Verified from the current [manifest](https://github.com/ipekbayrak/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/manifest.json):**

- `tabs`
- `storage`
- Host access to:
  - `https://www.youtube.com/*`
  - `https://gemini.google.com/*`
- Content scripts run continuously on both hosts.

The Store discloses collection/use of:

- Web history
- Website content

It also certifies that data is not sold, used outside core functionality, or used for lending/creditworthiness.

The repository [privacy policy](https://github.com/ipekbayrak/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) says settings plus pending URL/title/channel are stored in `chrome.storage.local`, with no analytics, tracking, or remote developer collection. Source inspection is consistent with that: no developer backend or analytics appears in the current repository. The resulting prompt is, however, deliberately submitted to Google Gemini.

**Unknown:** the Store-linked external policy at [ipekbayrak.com.tr/privacy-policy](https://ipekbayrak.com.tr/privacy-policy) did not expose extension-specific policy content during this research.

### YouTube surfaces

**Verified selectors in current [`youtube.js`](https://github.com/ipekbayrak/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/src/content/youtube.js):**

```text
ytd-rich-item-renderer
ytd-video-renderer
ytd-grid-video-renderer
ytm-shorts-lockup-view-model-v2
yt-lockup-view-model
ytd-compact-video-renderer
ytd-playlist-panel-video-renderer
```

It also injects into the watch-page action row using variants of:

```text
ytd-watch-metadata … #top-level-buttons-computed
ytd-watch-metadata #actions-inner
```

It observes the SPA using a throttled `MutationObserver`, `yt-navigate-finish`, and `yt-page-data-updated`.

**Inference, not an end-to-end guarantee:** these renderer types plausibly cover home feeds, search results, channel grids, Shorts shelves, related-video sidebars, playlist panels, and watch pages. No current automated browser test proves every named route, and YouTube can alter renderer structure independently. The transcript’s “homepage/search/channel/Shorts/video page” claim is reasonable but stronger than the evidence.

### Handoff, injection, and submission

The architecture is:

1. YouTube script extracts URL/title/channel.
2. Service worker saves `{id,url,title,channel,createdAt}` as `pendingPrompt` in `chrome.storage.local`.
3. It opens a new Gemini tab by default, or reloads/reuses one if configured.
4. Gemini content script renders the saved prompt template and manipulates the composer DOM.
5. It optionally finds and clicks Send.

Current editor fallbacks include:

```text
.ql-editor.textarea.new-input-ui[contenteditable="true"]
.ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]
div[contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"]
div[contenteditable="true"][aria-label*="prompt" i]
textarea[aria-label*="prompt" i]
```

Send fallbacks include:

```text
button.send-button.submit
button[aria-label*="send" i]
button[type="submit"]
```

The editor is polled for roughly six seconds. Submission uses a configurable 0–2000 ms delay and up to three button checks.

### Configuration and failures

**Verified configuration in `chrome.storage.local`:**

- Five built-in languages: English, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Turkish
- Custom `{title}`, `{channel}`, `{url}` template
- Auto-submit
- New/reused tab
- Hover-only controls
- Send delay

There is **no built-in Traditional Chinese option**; a user can still write a Traditional Chinese custom template.

**Failure behavior:**

- Missing editor or send button: retains the pending request and writes only a console warning.
- Signed-out/login flow: retained pending state can be retried on a later Gemini load.
- Invalidated extension context: disables YouTube buttons until reload.
- No visible clipboard/toast fallback.
- If auto-submit is disabled, the script fills the composer but leaves `pendingPrompt` stored.
- A write failure is swallowed before submission logic, so the code does not positively verify that the intended text reached the editor before clicking Send.

Thus the transcript correctly attributes clipboard fallback only to the second extension, not this one.

## 3. `wizdes/yt-gemini-summary`

### Matching source and permissions

The Store listing directly links [`wizdes/yt-gemini-summary`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary), and the name, version, workflow, prompt editor, ready indicator, and fallback all match. This is the discoverable second source repository.

Its [manifest](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/manifest.json) requests:

- `storage`
- `activeTab`
- `clipboardWrite`
- Host access to:
  - `https://www.youtube.com/*`
  - `https://m.youtube.com/*`
  - `https://gemini.google.com/*`

The Store says the developer does not collect or use user data and gives the same three no-sale/no-unrelated-use/no-credit certifications.

### Privacy discrepancy

The source contains no apparent analytics, ads, or developer server, and the policy correctly acknowledges that title/link are sent to Google Gemini.

However, its [privacy policy](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) says the saved prompt lives locally/on-device, while [`options.js`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/options.js) actually uses `chrome.storage.sync`.

According to Chrome’s official [Storage API documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/storage), `storage.sync` synchronizes to the user’s other signed-in Chrome instances when Chrome Sync is enabled. Therefore:

- “Nothing is sent to the developer” is consistent with source.
- “Only on this device” is inaccurate unless Chrome Sync is disabled.
- The built prompt handoff itself uses memory-only `chrome.storage.session`, which is cleared on browser restart, extension reload/update, or disable.

### YouTube surface and URL handling

This extension deliberately avoids YouTube renderer selectors:

- [`content-youtube.js`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/content-youtube.js) only reports URL changes so the toolbar icon can show a green ready dot.
- The toolbar click reads the active tab’s URL/title.
- On a search/home/channel page, clicking does nothing except show `YT?`.
- It does not inject controls into thumbnails, cards, or the watch-page action row.

Its pure URL helper accepts strict 11-character IDs from:

- `/watch?v=`
- `youtu.be`
- `/shorts/`
- `/live/`
- `/embed/`
- `/v/`
- mobile and music hosts

It canonicalizes them to `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID` and removes playlist, timestamp, and tracking parameters. Tests cover these cases in [`test/lib.test.mjs`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/test/lib.test.mjs).

### Handoff, injection, submission, and fallback

The [background worker](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/background.js):

1. Reads custom instructions from `chrome.storage.sync`.
2. Appends the cleaned title and canonical URL.
3. Saves `{prompt,ts}` in `chrome.storage.session`.
4. Always opens `https://gemini.google.com/app`.

The [Gemini script](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/content-gemini.js) waits up to 20 seconds for these visible editor candidates:

```text
rich-textarea .ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]
.ql-editor[contenteditable="true"]
div[contenteditable="true"][role="textbox"]
div[contenteditable="true"]
textarea
```

It fills with `execCommand('insertText')`, falling back to `textContent` plus an input event. It then waits up to eight seconds for:

```text
button.send-button
button[aria-label*="send" i]
button[mattooltip*="send" i]
button[data-test-id="send-button"]
```

Submission is always automatic; there is no auto-submit toggle or delay setting.

Pending state expires after ten minutes. Once an editor is found, it is removed **before** filling/submitting, preventing another Gemini tab from duplicating the request.

If injection or submission fails, it shows a toast with a read-only textarea plus **Copy** and **Dismiss**. Correction to the transcript/listing shorthand: it does not automatically write to the clipboard; clipboard access occurs only when the user presses Copy.

One concern is the very broad late fallback `div[contenteditable="true"]`, which could select the wrong editor if Gemini introduces another visible contenteditable element.

The README’s assertion that private/unlisted videos “fall back to the title and transcript” is **not implemented by this extension**: it does not obtain a transcript. That behavior, if it occurs at all, would belong to Gemini Web and was not verified in Google’s Apps documentation.

---

## 4. Gemini claims from the transcript

### Verified

- Gemini Apps officially supports finding YouTube videos/playlists/channels and answering questions about their content. It requires sign-in and Activity enabled ([Gemini Apps Help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16622858?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en)).
- The Gemini API explicitly accepts a public YouTube URL as a video input. The current documentation marks this **Preview**, allows up to ten videos for Gemini 2.5+, lists an eight-hour/day free-tier YouTube allowance, and says the paid tier has no limit based specifically on video length ([video-understanding documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video-understanding)).
- API video understanding uses sound and imagery and supports timestamp questions.

### Overstated or unverified

- The Apps help page does **not** document “paste any YouTube URL” as its prescribed workflow or provide a public/unlisted/private compatibility matrix. Therefore, the transcript’s conclusion that the user’s exact pasted-URL workflow is officially guaranteed goes beyond the cited Apps documentation.
- The API’s explicit URL support does not establish equivalent contractual behavior for the signed-in Gemini Web UI. API keys, quotas, billing, and endpoints are a separate integration path.

### Prompt-prefill deep link

No current official Gemini Apps help page located in this research documents a prompt-bearing URL such as:

```text
https://gemini.google.com/app?prompt=...
```

The official [Gemini usage page](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13275745?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en) documents opening Gemini, entering a prompt, and starting a new chat, but no `prompt`, `q`, launch, or prefill parameter.

This verifies the narrower claim **“there is no documented, supported prompt-prefill deep link.”** Absence from public documentation cannot prove that no internal or experimental scheme exists.

Third-party projects such as [`gaiar/gemini-url-prompt`](https://github.com/gaiar/gemini-url-prompt) accept `?prompt=` or `?q=`, but only because their own content script reads that parameter and injects it into Gemini. That is a workaround, not native Gemini behavior.

---

## 5. Lessons for a minimal cross-manager userscript MVP

Use the wizdes architecture as the baseline, not ipek’s full surface coverage:

1. **One userscript, two matches:** YouTube and Gemini. Use per-script GM storage for the handoff; no service worker or backend is needed.
2. **Start only on current `/watch` and `/shorts` pages.** Add a small fixed button or `GM_registerMenuCommand`. Do not initially support seven thumbnail/card renderers.
3. **Canonicalize the video ID.** Preserve only the 11-character ID and remove playlist/tracking/time parameters.
4. **Persist two separate classes of state:**
   - Long-lived preferences: Traditional Chinese prompt template and optional auto-submit.
   - Short-lived handoff: `{id,prompt,createdAt}`, with a five- or ten-minute TTL.
5. **Open plain `https://gemini.google.com/app`.** Do not depend on an undocumented query parameter.
6. **Prefill first; make auto-submit opt-in.** Manual Send removes the most fragile selector and reduces accidental submission. If enabled later, require visible/enabled controls and verify composer text first.
7. **Centralize ordered Gemini selectors.** Prefer specific Quill/role selectors; avoid accepting a generic `div[contenteditable]` without validating its role/ancestor.
8. **Never fail silently.** On timeout, show the complete prompt in a selectable toast with a user-initiated Copy button.
9. **Handle login and duplication explicitly:** retain pending state on a login route; claim/delete it only after finding the intended composer; show fallback if fill/send then fails.
10. **Keep grants minimal:** storage, deletion, and optionally menu/open-tab APIs. No `GM_xmlhttpRequest`, Gemini API key, transcript pipeline, analytics, or remote code.
11. **Test Tampermonkey and Violentmonkey separately:** legacy `GM_*` storage calls are synchronous in those managers, while `GM.*` storage APIs are Promise-based. A tiny wrapper prevents API-style differences ([Tampermonkey docs](https://www.tampermonkey.net/documentation.php?locale=en&q=GM_values), [Violentmonkey API](https://violentmonkey.github.io/api/gm/)).
12. **Defer full-product features:** homepage/search overlays, channel extraction, tab reuse, language selector UI, delay slider, multiple presets, transcript extraction, and Gemini API support.

This MVP retains the user’s existing Gemini Web account/session and provides the desired Traditional Chinese prompt while limiting maintenance to one YouTube route check, a small handoff state machine, and Gemini’s composer selectors.

## Inaccessible or unknown

- Exact byte-level contents of both Chrome Web Store packages.
- Whether current signed-in Gemini DOM automation succeeds in every account/UI experiment; no authenticated browser test was performed.
- Public install history or active-user telemetry beyond the Store’s displayed “users.”
- Permission-warning prose, which was absent from accessible Store page content; requested permissions were verified from source manifests.
- Any undocumented internal Gemini prefill scheme.
- Extension-specific content of ipek’s externally hosted Store privacy-policy URL.

Third-party mirrors already lag—for example, one still reports six rather than seven users for wizdes—so they should not override the direct Store values.\n\n### Version/activity corrections\n\n- **Verified:** ipek’s Store package remains **0.1.2**, while repository `main` is **0.1.3**. The three intervening commits add hover visibility, duplicate-watch-button reconciliation, Shadow DOM link discovery, and packaging changes ([comparison](https://github.com/ipekbayrak/yt-gemini-summary/compare/86ef108...1bc915b)). Therefore, some robustness described by current source is not necessarily in the Store build.\n- **Verified:** wizdes’s latest 2026-08-26 activity rewrites documentation/comments; the Gemini injector itself has not functionally changed since 2026-06-17, and background behavior since approximately 2026-06-18. Source inspection is consistent with that: no developer backend or analytics appears in the current repository. The resulting prompt is, however, deliberately submitted to Google Gemini.\n\n**Unknown:** the Store-linked external policy at [ipekbayrak.com.tr/privacy-policy](https://ipekbayrak.com.tr/privacy-policy) did not expose extension-specific policy content during this research.\n\n### YouTube surfaces\n\n**Verified selectors in current [`youtube.js`](https://github.com/ipekbayrak/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/src/content/youtube.js):**\n\n```text\nytd-rich-item-renderer\nytd-video-renderer\nytd-grid-video-renderer\nytm-shorts-lockup-view-model-v2\nyt-lockup-view-model\nytd-compact-video-renderer\nytd-playlist-panel-video-renderer\n```\n\nIt also injects into the watch-page action row using variants of:\n\n```text\nytd-watch-metadata … #top-level-buttons-computed\nytd-watch-metadata #actions-inner\n```\n\nIt observes the SPA using a throttled `MutationObserver`, `yt-navigate-finish`, and `yt-page-data-updated`.\n\n**Inference, not an end-to-end guarantee:** these renderer types plausibly cover home feeds, search results, channel grids, Shorts shelves, related-video sidebars, playlist panels, and watch pages. No current automated browser test proves every named route, and YouTube can alter renderer structure independently. The transcript’s “homepage/search/channel/Shorts/video page” claim is reasonable but stronger than the evidence.\n\n### Handoff, injection, and submission\n\nThe architecture is:\n\n1. YouTube script extracts URL/title/channel.\n2. Service worker saves `{id,url,title,channel,createdAt}` as `pendingPrompt` in `chrome.storage.local`.\n3. It opens a new Gemini tab by default, or reloads/reuses one if configured.\n4. Gemini content script renders the saved prompt template and manipulates the composer DOM.\n5. It optionally finds and clicks Send.\n\nCurrent editor fallbacks include:\n\n```text\n.ql-editor.textarea.new-input-ui[contenteditable=\"true\"]\n.ql-editor[contenteditable=\"true\"]\ndiv[contenteditable=\"true\"][role=\"textbox\"]\ndiv[contenteditable=\"true\"][aria-label*=\"prompt\" i]\ntextarea[aria-label*=\"prompt\" i]\n```\n\nSend fallbacks include:\n\n```text\nbutton.send-button.submit\nbutton[aria-label*=\"send\" i]\nbutton[type=\"submit\"]\n```\n\nThe editor is polled for roughly six seconds. Submission uses a configurable 0–2000 ms delay and up to three button checks.\n\n### Configuration and failures\n\n**Verified configuration in `chrome.storage.local`:**\n\n- Five built-in languages: English, Spanish, Hindi, Arabic, Turkish\n- Custom `{title}`, `{channel}`, `{url}` template\n- Auto-submit\n- New/reused tab\n- Hover-only controls\n- Send delay\n\nThere is **no built-in Traditional Chinese option**; a user can still write a Traditional Chinese custom template.\n\n**Failure behavior:**\n\n- Missing editor or send button: retains the pending request and writes only a console warning.\n- Signed-out/login flow: retained pending state can be retried on a later Gemini load.\n- Invalidated extension context: disables YouTube buttons until reload.\n- No visible clipboard/toast fallback.\n- If auto-submit is disabled, the script fills the composer but leaves `pendingPrompt` stored.\n- A write failure is swallowed before submission logic, so the code does not positively verify that the intended text reached the editor before clicking Send.\n\nThus the transcript correctly attributes clipboard fallback only to the second extension, not this one.\n\n---\n\n## 3. `wizdes/yt-gemini-summary`\n\n### Matching source and permissions\n\nThe Store listing directly links [`wizdes/yt-gemini-summary`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary), and the name, version, workflow, prompt editor, ready indicator, and fallback all match. This is the discoverable second source repository.\n\nIts [manifest](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/manifest.json) requests:\n\n- `storage`\n- `activeTab`\n- `clipboardWrite`\n- Host access to:\n  - `https://www.youtube.com/*`\n  - `https://m.youtube.com/*`\n  - `https://gemini.google.com/*`\n\nThe Store says the developer does not collect or use user data and gives the same three no-sale/no-unrelated-use/no-credit certifications.\n\n### Privacy discrepancy\n\nThe source contains no apparent analytics, ads, or developer server, and the policy correctly acknowledges that title/link are sent to Google Gemini.\n\nHowever, its [privacy policy](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/PRIVACY.md) says the saved prompt lives locally/on-device, while [`options.js`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/options.js) actually uses `chrome.storage.sync`.\n\nAccording to Chrome’s official [Storage API documentation](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/extensions/reference/api/storage), `storage.sync` synchronizes to the user’s other signed-in Chrome instances when Chrome Sync is enabled. Therefore:\n\n- “Nothing is sent to the developer” is consistent with source.\n- “Only on this device” is inaccurate unless Chrome Sync is disabled.\n- The built prompt handoff itself uses memory-only `chrome.storage.session`, which is cleared on browser restart, extension reload/update, or disable.\n\n### YouTube surface and URL handling\n\nThis extension deliberately avoids YouTube renderer selectors:\n\n- [`content-youtube.js`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/content-youtube.js) only reports URL changes so the toolbar icon can show a green ready dot.\n- The toolbar click reads the active tab’s URL/title.\n- On a search/home/channel page, clicking does nothing except show `YT?`.\n- It does not inject controls into thumbnails, cards, or the watch-page action row.\n\nIts pure URL helper accepts strict 11-character IDs from:\n\n- `/watch?v=`\n- `youtu.be`\n- `/shorts/`\n- `/live/`\n- `/embed/`\n- `/v/`\n- mobile and music hosts\n\nIt canonicalizes them to `https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ID` and removes playlist, timestamp, and tracking parameters. Tests cover these cases in [`test/lib.test.mjs`](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/test/lib.test.mjs).\n\n### Handoff, injection, submission, and fallback\n\nThe [background worker](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/background.js):\n\n1. Reads custom instructions from `chrome.storage.sync`.\n2. Appends the cleaned title and canonical URL.\n3. Saves `{prompt,ts}` in `chrome.storage.session`.\n4. Always opens `https://gemini.google.com/app`.\n\nThe [Gemini script](https://github.com/wizdes/yt-gemini-summary/blob/main/content-gemini.js) waits up to 20 seconds for these visible editor candidates:\n\n```text\nrich-textarea .ql-editor[contenteditable=\"true\"]\n.ql-editor[contenteditable=\"true\"]\ndiv[contenteditable=\"true\"][role=\"textbox\"]\ndiv[contenteditable=\"true\"]\ntextarea\n```\n\nIt fills with `execCommand('insertText')`, falling back to `textContent` plus an input event. It then waits up to eight seconds for:\n\n```text\nbutton.send-button\nbutton[aria-label*=\"send\" i]\nbutton[mattooltip*=\"send\" i]\nbutton[data-test-id=\"send-button\"]\n```\n\nSubmission is always automatic; there is no auto-submit toggle or delay setting.\n\nPending state expires after ten minutes. Once an editor is found, it is removed **before** filling/submitting, preventing another Gemini tab from duplicating the request.\n\nIf injection or submission fails, it shows a toast with a read-only textarea plus **Copy** and **Dismiss**. Correction to the transcript/listing shorthand: it does not automatically write to the clipboard; clipboard access occurs only when the user presses Copy.\n\nOne concern is the very broad late fallback `div[contenteditable=\"true\"]`, which could select the wrong editor if Gemini introduces another visible contenteditable element.\n\nThe README’s assertion that private/unlisted videos “fall back to the title and transcript” is **not implemented by this extension**: it does not obtain a transcript. That behavior, if it occurs at all, would belong to Gemini Web and was not verified in Google’s Apps documentation.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Gemini claims from the transcript\n\n### Verified\n\n- Gemini Apps officially supports finding YouTube videos/playlists/channels and answering questions about their content. It requires sign-in and Activity enabled ([Gemini Apps Help](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/16622858?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en)).\n- The Gemini API explicitly accepts a public YouTube URL as a video input. The current documentation marks this **Preview**, allows up to ten videos for Gemini 2.5+, lists an eight-hour/day free-tier YouTube allowance, and says the paid tier has no limit based specifically on video length ([video-understanding documentation](https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/video-understanding)).\n- API video understanding uses sound and imagery and supports timestamp questions.\n\n### Overstated or unverified\n\n- The Apps help page does **not** document “paste any YouTube URL” as its prescribed workflow or provide a public/unlisted/private compatibility matrix. Therefore, the transcript’s conclusion that the user’s exact pasted-URL workflow is officially guaranteed goes beyond the cited Apps documentation.\n- The API’s explicit URL support does not establish equivalent contractual behavior for the signed-in Gemini Web UI. API keys, quotas, billing, and endpoints are a separate integration path.\n\n### Prompt-prefill deep link\n\nNo current official Gemini Apps help page located in this research documents a prompt-bearing URL such as:\n\n```text\nhttps://gemini.google.com/app?prompt=...\n```\n\nThe official [Gemini usage page](https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13275745?co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop&hl=en) documents opening Gemini, entering a prompt, and starting a new chat, but no `prompt`, `q`, launch, or prefill parameter.\n\nThis verifies the narrower claim **“there is no documented, supported prompt-prefill deep link.”** Absence from public documentation cannot prove that no internal or experimental scheme exists.\n\nThird-party projects such as [`gaiar/gemini-url-prompt`](https://github.com/gaiar/gemini-url-prompt) accept `?prompt=` or `?q=`, but only because their own content script reads that parameter and injects it into Gemini. That is a workaround, not native Gemini behavior.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Lessons for a minimal cross-manager userscript MVP\n\nUse the wizdes architecture as the baseline, not ipek’s full surface coverage:\n\n1. **One userscript, two matches:** YouTube and Gemini. Use per-script GM storage for the handoff; no service worker or backend is needed.\n2. **Start only on current `/watch` and `/shorts` pages.** Add a small fixed button or `GM_registerMenuCommand`. Do not initially support seven thumbnail/card renderers.\n3. **Canonicalize the video ID.** Preserve only the 11-character ID and remove playlist/tracking/time parameters.\n4. **Persist two separate classes of state:**\n   - Long-lived preferences: Traditional Chinese prompt template and optional auto-submit.\n   - Short-lived handoff: `{id,prompt,createdAt}`, with a five- or ten-minute TTL.\n5. **Open plain `https://gemini.google.com/app`.** Do not depend on an undocumented query parameter.\n6. **Prefill first; make auto-submit opt-in.** Manual Send removes the most fragile selector and reduces accidental submission. If enabled later, require visible/enabled controls and verify composer text first.\n7. **Centralize ordered Gemini selectors.** Prefer specific Quill/role selectors; avoid accepting a generic `div[contenteditable]` without validating its role/ancestor.\n8. **Never fail silently.** On timeout, show the complete prompt in a selectable toast with a user-initiated Copy button.\n9. **Handle login and duplication explicitly:** retain pending state on a login route; claim/delete it only after finding the intended composer; show fallback if fill/send then fails.\n10. **Keep grants minimal:** storage, deletion, and optionally menu/open-tab APIs. No `GM_xmlhttpRequest`, Gemini API key, transcript pipeline, analytics, or remote code.\n11. **Test Tampermonkey and Violentmonkey separately:** legacy `GM_*` storage calls are synchronous in those managers, while `GM.*` storage APIs are Promise-based. A tiny wrapper prevents API-style differences ([Tampermonkey docs](https://www.tampermonkey.net/documentation.php?locale=en&q=GM_values), [Violentmonkey API](https://violentmonkey.github.io/api/gm/)).\n12. **Defer full-product features:** homepage/search overlays, channel extraction, tab reuse, language selector UI, delay slider, multiple presets, transcript extraction, and Gemini API support.\n\nThis MVP retains the user’s existing Gemini Web account/session and provides the desired Traditional Chinese prompt while limiting maintenance to one YouTube route check, a small handoff state machine, and Gemini’s composer selectors.\n\n## Inaccessible or unknown\n\n- Exact byte-level contents of both Chrome Web Store packages.\n- Whether current signed-in Gemini DOM automation succeeds in every account/UI experiment; no authenticated browser test was performed.\n- Public install history or active-user telemetry beyond the Store’s displayed “users.”\n- Permission-warning prose, which was absent from accessible Store page content; requested permissions were verified from source manifests.\n- Any undocumented internal Gemini prefill scheme.\n- Extension-specific content of ipek’s externally hosted Store privacy-policy URL."
